title: Sanitizer run
description: A machine-checkable record of one dynamic sanitizer run (V2-35): AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, ThreadSanitizer, MemorySanitizer or LeakSanitizer. A sanitizer finding is runtime evidence that a claim about memory or undefined behaviour is false, so the record carries how the run ended and the bytes it printed. L2 hashes the output, ties finished_at to the evidence date, and rejects a record that declares a clean run while the output carries a sanitizer finding line. The record does not prove that the build was instrumented, that the corpus exercised the claim, or that the sanitizer would have caught a different defect; without an external anchor a forger can rewrite the record and its output together (C-13).

tool.description: Sanitizer that instrumented the build. Lsan is listed separately because a leak-only run is not an address run.

version.description: Toolchain version, e.g. 'rustc 1.101.0-nightly'. A sanitizer's answer can change with the compiler and runtime version.

build_flags.description: Flags that instrumented the build, e.g. '-Zsanitizer=address'. A run without recorded instrumentation flags cannot be told apart from an ordinary test run.

command.description: Exact command that ran the instrumented tests, including the environment that set the flags.

exit_code.description: Process exit code. A non-zero code cannot support a non-open status.

finished_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset. Its local date must equal the evidence date.

output.description: Path to the captured sanitizer output, relative to --tool-output-root (default: the project root at --root), or a URL, in which case the hash is not checked.

output_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the output bytes. Lint check L2 verifies it.

status.description: How the run ended (V2-28 vocabulary). completed — the process exited before any bound; exit_code is the sanitizer's own. unverified — the run was cut short or the supervisor could not decide; it cannot support a non-open claim. failed — non-zero exit before the bound. error — the wrapper could not start or supervise the process.
